content.title: Exercise and follow-up recommendations for chronic heart failure

recommendations.recommendation: Exercise is recommended for all patients who are able in order to improve exercise capacity, quality of life (QOL), and reduce heart failure (HF) hospitalization.
recommendations.notes: Applies to patients able to adhere to exercise programme; physical conditioning improves exercise capacity and QOL.

recommendations.recommendation: A supervised, exercise-based, cardiac rehabilitation programme should be considered in patients with more severe disease, frailty, or with comorbidities.

footnotes.c: In those who are able to adhere to the exercise programme.

general_follow_up.summary: Patients with HF require follow-up even if symptoms are well controlled to optimize therapy, detect asymptomatic progression, and review comorbidities and advances in care.
general_follow_up.recommended_interval: At intervals no longer than 6 months for stable patients; more frequent after recent hospital discharge or during medication uptitration.
general_follow_up.care_delivery_notes: Whether stable patients must be followed by cardiologists is uncertain; primary care follow-up may be appropriate in some settings. HF specialist follow-up and use of quality improvement registries associated with higher rates of optimal therapy and improved outcomes.

ecg.recommendation: An ECG should be done annually to detect QRS prolongation and may identify conduction disturbances and atrial fibrillation (AF).
ecg.rationale: Detection of QRS prolongation may identify candidates for cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT).

echocardiography.recommendation: Serial echocardiography generally not necessary unless clinical deterioration occurs.
echocardiography.specific: An echocardiogram is advised 3–6 months after optimization of standard therapies for HFrEF to determine need for additional pharmacological agents or implanted devices.
